plot: The day after her hill lesson Pip sees a moving truck next door and hears a big box go 'plong', guesses 'piano' and tells Turbo, who mishears 'piranha'; Bertha turns it into a pirate and Grumpy adds a ship, so by sunset all Wheelburg fears the new neighbour; Bolt follows the story back car by car to Pip, whose 'piano' was itself only a guess, and the neighbour who arrives at sunset saying 'Ahoy!' is retired crossing guard Mrs. Maple, back from a ferry trip, with a real piano by the window; lesson: tell what you saw, not what you heard; then a box left on the street says 'For Inspector Bolt. From an old friend.'

script.title: Is a Pirate Moving In Next to Pip?

set.place: Bakery Lane next to Pip's house and Turbo's school corner, moving day afternoon until sunset

script.description: A moving truck, a mysterious plong, and a rumour that grows all over Wheelburg. Inspector Bolt #18

beats.say: Wait! Wait for me! Who is moving in next to my house?
Easy with the big one! Mind the black and white keys!
Pip raced all the way down the hill. Straight to the truck.
The moving truck was called Hal. He carried homes for a living.
Hello, Hal! Who's going to live here? A little car like me?
Can't tell you, little one. Movers keep secrets. Rule number one.
But she wants this by the window. To watch the school crossing.
Then Hal rolled the big box down his ramp.
Plong? What goes plong? Something big and heavy!
Big, heavy and plong. I bet it's a piano!
Pip never saw inside the box.
I have to tell somebody! Turbo! Turbo!
Turbo was at his school corner, stopping cars for the bell.
Stop! Wait! Go! Stop! Wait! Go! Best job ever!
Turbo! My new neighbour has a big piano! It goes plong!
Then Pip zoomed home. She didn't wait for an answer.
And just then, a big lorry honked. Turbo heard only half.
A big... piranha? A giant fish with teeth? Next to Pip?!
After school, Big Bertha pulled up to the corner.
Bertha! Pip's new neighbour keeps a giant piranha! Plong!
A piranha?! Oh my wheels! Who keeps a pet like that?
Only one kind of car keeps a piranha. A pirate!
Off went Bertha, telling every car she passed.
Grumpy was parked by the bakery, eating his quiet lunch.
Grumpy! A pirate is moving onto Bakery Lane! With a piranha!
A pirate. Hmph. Pirates come with ships.
Ships don't fit on Bakery Lane. I'll tow it to sea.
By the afternoon, the whole town was talking about it.
Inspector Bolt was polishing his hat when the honking began.
Bolt! A pirate is moving in! With a ship and a piranha!
A pirate? In Wheelburg? Before dinner?
Very well. Which one of you saw this pirate?
Nobody said a word. Everybody looked at everybody else.
Bolt! Everybody says my new neighbour is a pirate!
I wanted a friend next door. Now everyone is scared of her.
If they all shout pirate, she'll drive straight back home!
She arrives at sunset. That's when I give her the keys.
Then we find the truth before the sun goes down.
A story is like tyre tracks. Let's follow it back.
Bolt drove to the last car who heard it.
Grumpy. Who told you about the pirate ship?
Bertha said pirate. I added the ship. Ships make sense.
Bertha. Did you see a pirate with your own headlights?
Well, no. Turbo said piranha. And who keeps a piranha? A pirate!
Turbo. Did you see a piranha?
Not exactly. A lorry was honking. Pip said piranha. I think.
And every headlight in Wheelburg turned to look at Pip.
Me? I never said piranha! I said piano! Pi-a-no!
Piano. Piranha. Pirate. Oh no. They all start the same!
And I made a fish into a pirate. Oh, dear me.
One more question, Pip. Did you see a piano?
No. I heard a plong. And then I guessed.
So the very first piece of the story was a guess too.
Then nobody knows who she is! Not even me!
Just then, the sun touched the top of Wheelburg Hill.
Two headlights came slowly down Bakery Lane.
Everybody stay calm. Nobody say pirate.
Ahoy there, Wheelburg!
She said ahoy! Pirates say ahoy!
Wait! I know that voice! It's Mrs. Maple!
Hello, dear Pip! Sorry. I just came back from a ferry trip.
On the ferry, everybody says ahoy. It's a hard habit to stop.
The old crossing guard who gave Turbo his badge!
I moved close to the school. Now I can watch my crossing.
Your keys, Mrs. Maple. And your piano is by the window.
So it really was a piano! Not a pirate! Not a piranha!
A piranha? Goodness, no. I don't even own a goldfish.
Mrs. Maple rolled up to her piano. And she played.
Everybody honked along. Even Grumpy. Very, very quietly.
Mrs. Maple, I'm sorry. I called you a pirate all afternoon.
That's alright, Bertha. I've been called worse. A slowpoke, mostly.
Remember, everyone. Tell what you saw. Not what you heard.
Tell what you saw. Not what you heard. I'll remember!
And Pip, would you like piano lessons? Next door, every Friday?
A friend next door AND piano lessons? Yes, please!
Hal closed his doors. But one box stayed on the street.
On it, in big letters: For Inspector Bolt. From an old friend.
An old friend? Hmm. I wonder which one.
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
